title: Thailand vs Cambodia: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Thailand and Cambodia based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

faqs.question: Is Thailand or Cambodia better for first-time visitors to Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Thailand is the easier first trip. Tourism infrastructure is more developed — English signage is everywhere, the BTS/MRT in Bangkok is world-class, and accommodation ranges from $5 hostels to $500 resorts. Cambodia is more raw and adventurous, which seasoned travelers love, but it requires more flex

faqs.question: How far apart are Thailand and Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Bangkok to Siem Reap is about 400 km — a 1-hour flight ($60–100) or 8–10 hour bus via the Poipet border ($10–25). Bangkok to Phnom Penh is about 660 km — a 1h15m flight ($70–120). faqs.question: Is it worth visiting both on the same trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely, if you have 2+ weeks. A popular combo: 7–10 days Thailand (Bangkok + Chiang Mai or islands) plus 4–5 days Cambodia (Siem Reap for Angkor Wat + maybe Phnom Penh). faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Thailand or Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Cambodia is slightly cheaper on paper — $0.50 beers, $1 meals, $8 guestrooms. A mid-range day runs $20–40 vs Thailand's $30–50. faqs.question: Is Cambodia safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally safe. Siem Reap is very tourist-friendly with minimal crime. Phnom Penh requires more awareness — phone snatching from motorbikes is the main risk, so keep valuables in a front bag and avoid displaying expensive phones. faqs.answer: November through February — the cool, dry season with comfortable 25–33°C temperatures and virtually no rain. Peak tourist season, so prices are higher and popular spots get crowded.
